name: Masculism
scope: The masculist current as the scholarship on it describes it: the men's movement's claim that men as a sex are disadvantaged and that feminism is to blame (the self-label of Warren Farrell, who calls himself a men's liberationist 'or masculist'), a position Dupuis-Déri, Kemper's school and the Friedrich-Ebert and Heinrich-Böll foundations treat as a form of antifeminism. It excludes the sense of 'masculinism' that Brittan and Wood use for an ideology of patriarchy or male supremacy, and religious men's movements, since no defining source ties Farrell's texts to them. It holds positions on gender, family and violence only, so statements on other topics have no answer.

sources.title: Le « masculinisme » : une histoire politique du mot (en anglais et en français)
sources.author: Francis Dupuis-Déri, Recherches féministes 22(2), 2009
sources.usedFor: The history of the words masculism and masculinism, Farrell's self-label, and the contested meaning.

sources.title: The Myth of Male Power: Why Men Are the Disposable Sex (Random House, 1993/1994; archive.org scan)
sources.author: Warren Farrell
sources.usedFor: The key work: Farrell's account of men as the disposable sex, and his proposed Equal Rights and Responsibilities Amendment.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Farrell calls male-only draft registration and combat requirements the most unconstitutional laws in America under the Fourteenth Amendment and proposes an amendment to outlaw male-only legal responsibilities (ch. 5, p. 94; Conclusion, p. 263).

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Farrell objects that the Violence against Women Act funds women's shelters and none for men, and that only women testified (ch. 9, p. 160); he says two-sex studies find women and men equally likely to initiate domestic violence and that battered men are ashamed to report (ch. 9, p. 190).

equal-conscription.rationale: Farrell calls male-only draft registration unconstitutional and proposes an Equal Rights and Responsibilities Amendment that would outlaw male-only responsibility for draft registration and require combat obligations of both sexes (ch. 5, pp. 92-94, 112; Conclusion, p. 263).

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Farrell argues that depriving fathers and sons of their right to live because of their sex violates the Fourteenth Amendment's guarantee of equal protection, and wants equal rights and responsibilities in law (ch. 5, p. 94; Conclusion, p. 263).

equal-parenting.rationale: Farrell expects fathers to seek to remove judges who award more than 60 percent of contested custody cases to either sex, and his proposed amendment cuts funds where judges give women more than 60 percent (ch. 'Conclusion', pp. 260, 263); he asks for no flat equal-time presumption.

evolved-behavioural-sex-differences.rationale: Farrell writes that the myth of male power violates both sexes' 'biologically inherited instinct to protect the female' (Introduction to the book, p. 10); he gives no wider account of sex differences.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Farrell proposes an Equal Life Opportunity Commission on the model of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission and an Office of Equal Male Life (Conclusion, pp. 262-263), and criticises agencies that serve only women (Introduction, p. 6; ch. 7, p. 132).

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Farrell notes an Office of Research on Women's Health with no office for men's health (ch. 7, p. 132) and proposes an Equal Life Opportunity Commission for suicide, disease and the other 'glass cellars' of men (Conclusion, pp. 262-263).

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Farrell proposes a paradigm shift from a male-dominated, patriarchal, sexist world to one that was 'bi-sexist', both male- and female-dominated, both patriarchal and matriarchal, each in different ways (Introduction, pp. 4-5; ch. 3).

summary: Masculism, as the scholarship on it describes it, is the current that treats men as a sex disadvantaged by conscription, custody rulings, early death, suicide and violence, and that holds feminism responsible; Dupuis-Déri and the Böll and Ebert foundations class it as antifeminism. Its key work, Warren Farrell's The Myth of Male Power, rejects the idea of a male-dominated patriarchy, calls the world 'bi-sexist', and asks for equal rights and equal responsibilities, including a draft for both sexes and men's shelters and health offices.

notes: Searched the key work (The Myth of Male Power) for the draft, custody, domestic violence, patriarchy, affirmative action, abortion, pornography, prostitution, divorce law, voting, pay, health and government agencies. The other defining sources (Dupuis-Déri, Böll, FES, Blais) describe the term and say nothing on the statements. Farrell's key-figure listing belongs to the men's rights movement entry, so his shorter web texts aren't cited. Statements on economy, state, world and ecology are null: masculism has no doctrine there. Page numbers are those printed in the archive.org scan, approximate near chapter breaks.
